text:
claire: Observed in the shard-reassign soak: some queue entries become 'orphaned' after handoff. They stay in evict queue and never reach the new owner; memory creeps. Small log snippet attached.

oscar: paste pls

claire:
[handoff] claim shard=9 epoch=201 -> ok
[handoff] transfer prefix=acct/77/bar release -> ack_sent
[evict] enqueue prefix=acct/77/bar id=0x7a -> ENQUEUED (owner=old-node)
[handoff] new-owner bind shard=9 epoch=202 -> ok
[evict] dequeue id=0x7a -> not-found (index lookup owner mismatch)

mei: looks like queue indexing is owner-bound. when owner changes, the dequeue path can't locate entries.

ben: options: 1) stable enqueue key (prefix + enqueue-id) so entries are owner-agnostic; 2) add small ledger mapping enqueue-id -> owner-epoch; 3) background reaper to sweep unreachable entries.

oscar: stable-key seems cleanest long-term. Ledger helps incremental rollout but adds distributed state. Reaper is least invasive but only eventual.

mei: operational concerns: need global dedupe for enqueue-id (CAS on primary index) to avoid duplicates during retries across epochs. Also tombstone handling: tombstones must always be allowed to short-circuit even if epochs differ.

claire: mitigation plan: enable a slow reaper in prod (low QPS) and flip a canary node to stable-key enqueue to measure enqueue latency and CAS conflict rate. Add metrics orphaned_queue_entries, enqueue_cas_conflicts, enqueue_latency_p95.

ben: migration sketch: dual-write for a short window, backfill existing rows with enqueue-ids via a background rewriter, then switch primary index. Need a brief pause-enqueue window for the final cutover.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: stable-enqueue-key.v1 on canary-3 at 2026-03-23T18:05:00Z

oscar: also add tombstone-epoch on tombstone messages and require tombstone.epoch >= enqueue.origin_epoch to apply. Add tombstone_ttl guard.

claire: I'll open the canary PR with smoke tests (handoff storm + tombstone race) and the ops dashboard. tagging reviewers. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary rollout healthy: stable-enqueue-key.v1 (ok)

mei: if canary looks good we'll draft RFC outlining stable-key, migration steps, cost (index size), and benchmarks.

claire: thanks everyone. scheduling chaos run next week to validate.
